To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The first 4 months of life are the most critical time for developing tolerance to foreign antigens.
The use of fetal gene transfer to induce tolerance is a safe and effective strategy.

(1) The first trimester fetal sheep is a good model for studying tolerance induction; (2) Early gene delivery to the fetus induces both central and peripheral tolerance; (3) The central tolerance mechanism involves a deletion of the T cell receptor repertoire; (4) The peripheral tolerance mechanism is mediated through the induction of T regulatory cells; and (5) T regulatory cell function can be enhanced by the addition of IL-2 to the gene delivery construct.

the mechanisms by which the immune system is able to recognize self and foreign antigens and to mount an immune response to foreign antigens.
